title: Hazelnut and chocolate chip scones
subtitle: classic cream scones with skinned hazelnuts and dark chocolate chips
excerpt: These scones use the rubbing-in method with double cream instead of milk, which gives a richer, more tender crumb. Dark chocolate chips and toasted skinned hazelnuts are the additions. The scones are round and domed, not layered: the method is the same as a plain cream scone, with the additions folded in at the end.
sourceNotes: Chocolate chip and hazelnut scone, a contemporary British variation on the classic cream scone. Method from standard British home-baking practice.

glossaryTerms.definition: A scone made with double cream in place of butter and milk. The fat in the cream coats the flour and keeps the crumb tender without requiring the rubbing-in step.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked scones once cool. Reheat from frozen at 180°C fan for 10 to 12 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Best eaten on the day. Cut unbaked scones can be refrigerated overnight and baked fresh.

with a very tender, biscuit-like crumb. Toast the hazelnuts in a dry pan until golden and the skins begin to blister, then rub off the skins in a clean tea towel while still warm. Cooled, toasted hazelnuts are much more fragrant than raw ones in the finished scone.

items.prepNote: toasted, skins rubbed off, roughly chopped

content.text: Heat the oven to 200°C fan. Line a baking tray with baking parchment.
Mix the flour, baking powder, caster sugar, and salt in a large bowl. Add the cold butter and rub in with your fingertips until the mixture looks like coarse crumbs.

Stir in the chocolate chips and chopped hazelnuts. Pour in the double cream and milk, then mix with a table knife until a rough dough just comes together. If the dough is very dry, add 1 tablespoon of milk.
Turn onto a lightly floured surface and pat into a disc about 3 cm thick. Stamp out rounds with a 6 cm cutter, pressing straight down without twisting. Re-pat the offcuts once.

Place on the tray and brush the tops with a little milk. Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until risen, golden on top, and set when pressed lightly at the side. Transfer to a wire rack. Best eaten warm within a few hours.

attrs.problem: Chocolate chips melting and bleeding into the dough before baking
attrs.avoid: Avoid over-mixing; the friction of too much handling warms the dough and softens the chips.
attrs.fix: Add the chips to the dry mixture before the cream, so they are distributed quickly. Keep mixing to a minimum.

attrs.problem: Scones very pale on top even after stated bake time
attrs.avoid: Avoid skipping the milk glaze; it browns the crust.
attrs.fix: If still pale at 18 minutes, switch the oven to grill/broil function for the final 2 minutes to colour the tops.
